audience: Developers, infrastructure engineers, SREs, and technically curious daily-game players.
hypothesis: A 30–60 second daily routing puzzle can earn repeat play, voluntary sharing, and credible sponsor interest without obstructive advertising.

verified_facts.claim: Packet Panic gives the player no more than six hops to reach the destination.
Every UTC date produces one deterministic graph with at least one valid route and a deliberate losing route.
The game requires no account and stores gameplay progress locally in the browser.
The intended play time is approximately 30–60 seconds.
The public experiment uses a fourteen-day validation window and a predeclared decision scorecard.

tone_constraints: Write as Abhinav in plain, technically literate language.
Introduce Cramzz as a recurring series about building small internet experiments in public.
State that the experiment may fail when discussing validation.
Tailor replies to the exact parent post.
sponsor_disclosure: Use “Sponsored” for paid placements. In unsponsored company outreach, say “No affiliation” when the context could imply endorsement.
